data.description:
Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:1787) ) has provided an announcement.

Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd. has approved the creation of Hong Kong Treasury Company, a new treasury vehicle jointly invested by its wholly owned subsidiary Mining Hong Kong and Yacheng Company, a wholly owned unit of controlling shareholder Gold Group Co. The venture will have total subscribed capital of RMB1 billion, with Yacheng holding 60% and Mining Hong Kong 40%, and the new entity will not be consolidated into Shandong Gold’s financial statements.

The establishment of Hong Kong Treasury Company is classified as a connected transaction under Hong Kong Listing Rules, triggering reporting and announcement requirements but exempting the deal from circular and independent shareholder approval. Post-establishment, the group plans to use the treasury company for daily financial cooperation, including cash pooling, deposits, settlement, credit services and foreign exchange and interest rate risk management, signalling a move to centralise and enhance its financial operations while maintaining regulatory compliance.

data.title: Low Uptake in Partial Offer Leaves Fu Shou Yuan Ownership Largely Unchanged
data.description:
Fu Shou Yuan International Group ( (HK:1448) ) has issued an update.

Fu Shou Yuan International Group Limited, a Hong Kong-listed Cayman Islands company in the death care and cemetery services sector, provides burial plots and related funeral services primarily to customers in mainland China. Its integrated service offering and listed status make shareholding changes and corporate actions significant for investors and for the group’s positioning in a specialized but important market.

Ms. Gong Hailin’s unconditional voluntary cash partial offer to acquire up to 115 million shares in Fu Shou Yuan closed with acceptances for only about 4.59 million shares, representing roughly 0.20 percent of the company’s issued capital. As the acceptances were far below the maximum, each accepting shareholder will have all tendered shares taken up at HK$0.10 per share, with settlement due within seven business days, while an odd-lot matching arrangement will operate off-market for six weeks despite the ongoing trading suspension.
